title: Two Steps for a Doubled Bit
statement: Let $x$ be a binary string, $s$ a syntax-scanner state, $i$ a natural number, and $b$ a bit. Suppose $i+2\le |x|$ and the bits of $x$ at positions $i$ and $i+1$ are both $b$. Starting from the verifier configuration on $x$ in the syntax state carrying $s$, with $i$ input bits consumed, empty work tape, and work head at $0$, after two steps the configuration is in the syntax state carrying the state reached by applying two syntax transitions on the doubled bit $bb$, with $i+2$ input bits consumed, empty work tape, and work head at $0$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be an input with $i + 2 \le |x|$ whose bits at positions $i$ and $i + 1$ both
equal $b$, and let $s$ be a formula-scanner state with transition $\delta$. Started in
the syntax state carrying $s$ with $i$ input bits consumed, empty work tape, work head
$0$, and empty output, the non-tautology verifier reaches, after exactly two steps,
the syntax state carrying $\delta(s, b)$ with $i + 2$ bits consumed and all else
unchanged.
